paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: The effect of context masking perturbations by tag. Error bars indicate the standard deviation.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the effect of context masking perturbations on multilingual BERT models, grouped by morphosyntactic tag: case, gender, number, and tense. The vertical axis represents the "effect" on a linear scale ranging from 0 to 20, with tick marks at intervals of 5. The horizontal axis lists the four tag categories in order from left to right. For each tag, there are six bars corresponding to different BERT models: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light red), and XLM-B₂ (dark red), as indicated in the legend. Error bars above and below each bar represent the standard deviation. In the "case" category, the effect values are highest, with mBERT-B₂ (light red) reaching approximately 12 and XLM-B₂ (dark red) around 11, while the other models show lower effects, mostly below 7. In "gender," all models exhibit small effects, mostly below 3, with mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ slightly higher. For "number," the effects are similarly low, with values near or below 2 for all models. In "tense," the effects are minimal for all models, with most bars barely rising above 0 and error bars indicating low variability. The bars are arranged in a grouped layout, with each group containing six bars in the same order as specified in the legend. No specific bars are visually emphasized beyond the standard error bars.
